name: painting_deep
note: A drawn painting at deep: a figure, a clock and a candle in cool light, the critique naming one craft decision.

thoughts.text: A person in their thirties, hair straight, face sad, standing in a green gown.
A river bank at blue hour. A clock hangs over them, and the clock is the same color as a candle nearby.
Rim light traces the edge of the figure, a thin bright outline against the darkening water. In paint, a single stroke of pale color would do it.
Green and blue dominate, cool on cool. The clock matching a candle adds one warm echo, so time and flame are tied by color.
A frame inside the frame: the clock, or an arch, boxes the figure in and gives the layered depth of a stage set.
Standing still beneath a clock, sad at the blue hour: the day, and something else, is ending. The mood is mournful.
The gown, the water and the sky stay in one cool family, so the sadness in the face is not fought by any bright note in the frame.
For a gallery wall: slow, low in energy, asking the viewer to wait with the figure. Fine art rather than illustration.
A loss, and its cause a letter that came this afternoon: the standing still is what comes after reading it.
Put the figure in full sun and the clock becomes a timetable. In the blue hour it becomes a verdict.

wordings.text: A person in their thirties with straight hair and a sad face stands in a green gown under a clock beside a candle of the same color, on a river bank at blue hour, rim-lit.

painting, person in their 30s, straight hair, sad expression, green gown, standing, under a clock, clock the same color as a candle, river bank at blue hour, rim light, waist up, frame in frame, mournful mood
1other, solo, straight hair, sad, green gown, standing, clock, candle, river, blue hour, rim lighting, upper body

The thin rim of light and the cool greens give the figure a sorrow that never raises its voice. The candle matching the clock is a good idea executed too literally; let the match stay a whisper so the figure stays the subject.
